recentItems.title: John Dickerson: how I learned to be more graceful to myself and others
recentItems.description:
John Dickerson made a name for himself as an anchor at CBS News. Last year, he left the world of broadcast news to pursue stories that put his values of generosity, curiosity and integrity at the core of his work. He talks to Rachel about remembering his own mortality and forging his own independent path in the world of journalism.

WHAT IS “WILD CARD?”
Life’s too short for small talk. NPR's Rachel Martin gets right to the questions that matter most. Once a week, famous guests pull questions from a deck of cards and open up about the kind of stuff we all think about but rarely say out loud. 

Actors, authors and thinkers are prompted to talk about everything from their insecurities and dreams to grief and God. Named one of The New York Times’ 10 best podcasts of 2024, Wild Card stands out among celebrity interview podcasts. When modern life feels chaotic or overwhelming, listen to Wild Card for a joyful, grounding reminder of our shared humanity. You can reach out to us at wildcard@npr.org. We love it when you do.

recentItems.title: Gillian Anderson shares how she got her life back on track after "many years" of feeling lost
recentItems.description:
"How am I complicit in not getting what I say that I want?” This is the question Gillian Anderson wants you to ask yourself. She has read many accounts from women detailing their sexual desires and disappointments, and she is sharing their stories with the world, a second time. Her newest book is called “More: Sexual Fantasies by Anonymous.”

recentItems.title: Nick Offerman, actor and writer, reflects on the death of Wendell Berry
recentItems.description:
Writer and environmentalist Wendell Berry died on Monday at age 92.

In an interview with Rachel Martin on NPR's Wild Card last year, actor and writer Nick Offerman reflected on Berry's legacy.

Watch the full interview at the link in bio.

recentItems.title: Sara Bareilles wants more people talking about infertility (and fewer people giving advice)
recentItems.description:
“Being a human is so complicated for so many reasons,” Sara Bareilles tells Rachel. That’s why she’s trying to show more grace for both herself and others these days. In Sara’s new album and documentary, both titled “Good Grief,” she’s processing the loss of dear friends, and her struggles with infertility. She also tells Rachel about becoming an unapologetic crier, and outgrowing low rise jeans.

recentItems.title: Brittany Howard on the lesson she had to learn about love: "Love doesn't always feel nice"
recentItems.description:
“We’re all gentler and we’re more sensitive,” Brittany Howard tells Rachel about reuniting with her band, Alabama Shakes. The band is back with their first studio album in over a decade, “I Must Be Dreaming.” Brittany talks with Rachel about why now was the right time to reunite, and how growing up poor influences her music to this day. She also talks about finding peace in hard work and why she loves the sound of a box fan.

recentItems.title: John Leguizamo reflects on the vulnerability he had to bring to his role in "The Odyssey"
recentItems.description:
John Leguizamo reflects on the vulnerability he had to bring to his role in "The Odyssey," and why it felt so special to him.

On this week’s Wild Card, he talks about growing up in an immigrant household and how he’s used his ADHD as an acting “superpower.”
